title: Hot Cocoa Mix

drivers.name: Heatwave (38°C forecast)
drivers.evidence: Historical heatwaves correlate with reduced hot cocoa demand; no prior heatwave-weeks show uplift; product is temperature-sensitive; planner note explicitly signals demand risk.

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: Past weeks at 5.20 price show no uplift (median 27–32, vs baseline 30.1); no promotional lift observed; price increase likely deters buyers.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 30.1. No events or promotions are planned. The price is raised 3.4% above regular (5.20 vs 5.03), which historically has not driven uplift—past 5.20 weeks show no consistent lift. The heatwave (38°C) is a strong demand deterrent for hot cocoa. Recent weeks at 5.20 price (2026-09-28 to 2026-10-05) show only marginal lift (median 27–32), consistent with baseline trends. No post-promo dip is observed. The heatwave overrides any seasonal tailwind. The classical model's x1.0 is correct; judgment confirms a downside effect from the heatwave.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 30.1 | 5%-95%: 10.6 - 42.6 | 10%-90%: 14.0 - 42.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
